text.p: Diversified manufacturer Hills Industries Ltd was on track for an improved profit in 1996/97, compared with the previous year, managing director David Simmons said on Friday.
"I think we are on track to do better than last year," Simmons told reporters after the company's annual general meeting.
Simmons said it was difficult to forecast the full year profit based on four months trading and added that November had not been as buoyant as the company had expected.
"But we are tracking above last year for the four months and our budgets suggest we should be able to deliver a reasonable result in the full year," he said.
Simmons said that underpinning the improved performance so far this year was Hills' supply contract to regional pay-tv operator Austar, whose roll-out had been stronger than Hills anticipated.
Hills would have gradual improvement in its consumer business, which was already evident, while its electronics unit, which fuelled last year's profit growth, had remained strong, he said.
At this stage the industrial business was a little below expectations for the year because of its exposure to the housing cycle, he said.
Simmons said Hills was keen on sensible acquisitions in any of its three businesses, but its priority would be electronics.
"Our plan is to get revenues around about the same amount out of each of the three segments," he said.
Hills achieved a 1.5 percent rise in 1995/96 (July/June) net profit to A$12.22 million after sales rose to A$338.72 million from A$300.95 million. Shares in Hills closed steady at A$8.10.
